_doc: The failure-class index (#4122, chairman 2026-10-08). A CLASS is a way the org fails that has happened more than once; the question asked of every defect before it closes is 'where else can this occur, and what stops it everywhere?'. THIS FILE HOLDS DEFINITIONS ONLY: id, name, guard. An INSTANCE is a closed row carrying the label class:<id>, counted by the gate, so a defect PR never edits this file (every PR appending here would hold every other by file overlap). A second closed row under one class:<id> is a REPEAT, and a repeat means the guard failed. `seed` lists the instances named when the file was written, with the BASIS for each: 'chairman-named' (the chairman's direction on #4122; class membership not re-read by ceo), 'title states it' (ceo read the row title, which says so), 'ceo read'. Re-read the row before relying on a seed. `guard` is a detector or rule IN FORCE that stops the class everywhere, or null with a guardNote saying what is missing or still unmerged: a control that is ordered, open or partial is a guardNote, never a guard. A class with a null guard is the first thing to fix. An instance with no row number (a pull request in another repository) is written <owner/name>#<n>. EVENT KINDS (#4450, epic #4437 move 1a): the entries from `main-red` on are EVENT kinds, not row defects. They have no `class:<id>` label and no closed rows: an instance is a line of the host's `failure-ledger` (`<kind>\t<ts ms>\t<ref>`), and a repeat is one kind with two or more distinct refs (`repeatsIn`).

classes.name: `main` is red: a trunk run of the code repository failed. Recorded per red RUN by the tick (`readTrunkRed`).
classes.guard: `readTrunkRed` in `src/trunk-red.ts` of a11ign/agent-org reads a declared code repository's newest `push` and `schedule` runs (`CODE_REPOSITORY_EVENT_FILTERS`, one call each, the newest of either deciding) and counts as red `main` a red push run, a red `cross-repo` leg whose `gate` read green (`continue-on-error` keeps the run and the required check green, so the leg's own job conclusion is read), and a red nightly. `trunkRedOrders` then wakes the fixer WITH the answer: the merging session of the newest commit with `product-manager` as its way out, and `product-manager` for a nightly, which has no commit of its own. Row a11ign/agent-org#539, merged as a11ign/agent-org#650 (2026-10-10T12:32:14Z). `src/trunk-red.test.ts` in agent-org pins it, each read with a negative control: the leg green, a repository with no such leg, a job that only contains the words, a refused runs read, and a green push or nightly that clears an older red. It stands in force since that merge; before it a red leg or nightly went unowned for 11 pushes.
classes.guardNote: recorder: the tick, from #4450 (`mainRedEvents` in `src/failure-ledger.ts` of agent-org, the episode rule from agent-org#674). ONE event per episode: the ref is the run that OPENED the red, and a standing red (a `cross-repo` leg red on every push, say) continues with no new event until a green reading ends it, so a later red is a new event even for the same job. A red naming a job the standing red did not is a new event, and a reading that was not read changes nothing. The standing red is kept in `failure-ledger-main-red` beside the ledger, so it survives the tick's fresh process. Row #4833 was filed from two per-run events of one red leg (lab runs 38045596539 and 38055200478 were one red `checks (cross-repo)` leg, not two). A leg is found by the NAME `cross-repo` (`CROSS_REPO_LEG`), so a `continue-on-error` job of another name reads green, and only a repository declared as a code repository (`trunkOfCodeRepository`, read by `scopeTick`) is read at all. A stuck agent-org red is reported, not escalated to `answer:ceo` (`stuckRowOf` reads `pr-<n>` as a row of the primary). The leg and repository rules are as of agent-org `origin/main` a6d68f5f, 2026-10-10; the episode rule was re-read on 2026-10-13 at agent-org `origin/main` 791aa07a.

classes.guardNote: Not covered: `readProseAndOrder` is the only `answer:<session>` writer found (by reading every `answer:` string in `src/` of agent-org), so a writer added elsewhere, or a label added by hand or by a one-shot script, does not pass through the guard. The label names the comment's AUTHOR, not the handoff's target (noted on #4679, not repaired). The writer of the 2026-10-09 burst was never positively identified in the journal; it is inferred to be `readProseAndOrder` replaying past labels, so a repeat from another path would not be refused.

classes.name: A claimed worker stopped mid-task, or a stalled holder or a spare held the slot a ready row needed, and nothing woke it or started another.
classes.guard: Two merged controls in a11ign/agent-org: #597 (row #458) wakes a claimed worker that is `idle` or `done` with a claim naming a branch, no open pull request, no pending check and no declared wait field, with a "continue" order after 10 minutes (`STOPPED_CLAIMANT_MINUTES`), tells a holder whose agent-session id changed that its background tasks are lost (`src/idle-claimant-stopped.test.ts`, `src/claim-stall-restart-notice.test.ts`), and writes its `claimed-worker-stalled` line to the failure ledger from the release that follows a nudge nothing answered, ref `<session>/#<row>/<nudge time>`, not from the nudge itself (corrected by #660, row #4826: `src/claimed-worker-stalled-ledger.test.ts`); #599 (row #459) types a spare `worker-<n>` only the row it was named for (`ownRowOnly` in `wake.ts`), so an unclaimed ready row starts a FRESH worker rather than a second row being typed into a standing session (`src/ready-row-dispatch.test.ts`).
classes.guardNote: Not covered: the 10-minute figure is capped below the measured healthy-wait tail (p90 11.3, p95 16.5 minutes), so some healthy waits draw one unneeded "continue" (#597 counted 18 of 146 in three weeks); a holder that has an open pull request or a declared wait stays on the 45-minute idle and 120-minute no-progress clocks; the 10-minute rule was replayed on four workers of #4437, not read on a live tick when #597 merged. A ledger line is not a nudge: it is written by the release that follows a nudge nothing answered (a holder released with its work kept), so two lines are two UNANSWERED nudges, and a `class-repeat` reading of this class IS a guard that did not bring a worker back, not the guard working. Still not seen: a `Claimed-nothing:` claim and a holder with an open pull request of its own are never released, so an unanswered nudge to one is in the wake ledger only (`<session>/claim-stalled/row-<n>/nudge-<ms>`). Still OFFERED: a `ready` row whose only wait is a body `Waiting-for:` line (no `blockedBy` edge, no `answer:` label, not `parked`) is not excused by a11ign/agent-org#597, so it is claimed and nudged again and again with nothing to build (a11ign#5156, three claims); the offer-pool fix is `partitionUnclaimed` reading body waits (a11ign/agent-org#1075), and until that merges the remedy is a native edge or `parked`.

classes.name: The trace store goes stale while sessions are working, so nobody reads the org's own metrics and nobody is told.
classes.guard: Merged controls in a11ign/agent-org: #498 gives the trace store a clock of its own, `a11ign-trace-ingest.timer` (`host/trace-ingest.timer.in`, every five minutes, `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`), which runs `src/trace/freshness.ts`. That file ingests (`trace -- --ingest`) and then asks whether the store is stale: a transcript has a turn-producing message that is 10 to 20 minutes old (`OWED_AFTER_MS` and `OWED_WINDOW_MS`, the chairman's ten minutes on a11ign#4437) and has no `turn` of its own in the store. A stale store raises ONE incident per episode, a comment on the standing row #928 and an order to the owning seat (`orchestrator`) under `Class: metrics-outage`, each effect retried next run if refused. The detector was corrected after its first three occurrences proved to be false positives on a healthy store (a11ign#4871): "working" is a transcript whose newest MESSAGE line is inside the window, not a touched file (#704, merged as #706, 2026-10-10 18:48Z), and the newest turn is read back past an old tail until one inside the window turns up, so a cold start is not read as stale (#709, merged as #739, 2026-10-10 20:37Z). The detector was corrected a third time (agent-org#1570, merged as agent-org#1571, 2026-10-16 10:25Z), the metrics-outage repeat that the ledger on #928 read as a false positive: `orchestrator`'s message at 09:17:47Z began an 8 min 40 s tool call (the Ansible wait), its result landed at 09:26:27Z, the store was read at 09:31:34Z, and the newest turn was 09:19:19Z, 12 minutes old, on a healthy store (ingest `276 events added, 0 failed`). STALE is an owed message with no turn, not no turn in ten minutes, so a session inside one long tool call that writes no message is not an outage, and a tool result owes nothing. Pinned in `src/trace/freshness.test.ts` (the touched-transcript case, the HELD BACK case and its positive control, the COLD START cases and their positive control, the once-per-episode cases) and the unit's wiring in `src/host-units.ts` / `src/packaging/host-units.test.ts`.
classes.guardNote: Not covered: the check lives in the same unit it watches, so a timer that is disabled or a host that is down raises nothing; a message is checked only while it is 10 to 20 minutes old, so an ingest that stays broken past that raises nothing for that message, and a session in one tool call that began more than 20 minutes after its last turn-producing message raises nothing until the call returns and writes one (a running call is not read as dead, but an outage that starts inside such a call is not reported until it returns); a healthy store reads up to about five minutes old (a turn is held back until its message is 5 minutes old, then waits for the next ingest); the incident is one comment and one order per episode, so nothing confirms the seat acted on it. Read from agent-org origin/main and its test file, not from a live incident: no genuine stale episode has been observed raised end to end since the two corrections, and the three occurrences on the ledger (2026-10-10 11:53Z, 15:00Z, 17:50Z) were the over-firing the corrections remove.

classes.name: A declared repo-wide sweep outlasts its CI-fix box and holds the lock, shelving every other row whose Region shares a file with it.
classes.guard: The sweep window in a11ign/agent-org `src/sweep-window.ts` (a11ign#4603, lock-gridlock fix 2 of 4; split by agent-org#1314): CI-fix time is boxed at `SWEEP_CI_BOX_MINUTES` (60) from the pull request opening, and past it the window is `overrun` and RELEASED BY CONSTRUCTION -- the freeze stops refusing other claims, the holder is told `revert or split; do not hold the lock` in a comment on the row, and the release is counted ONCE under the failure-ledger kind `sweep-window-released` (`SWEEP_WINDOW_RELEASED_KIND`, `src/failure-ledger.ts`), a counter that is no class and no repeat, because a released overrun is the guard working. `sweep-overrun` is written only for the failure the class names: a claim REFUSED on a swept Region AFTER its overrun notice (`row-claim.ts`, final verdict only), ref = the refused row. `src/sweep-window-overrun-kind.test.ts` reads both back from the ledger, with the refusal as the control.

classes.name: The `priority:chairman` label, which only the chairman's login may add, is put on a row by another login, so someone is claiming the chairman's authority over the queue.
classes.guard: The work gate in a11ign/agent-org (`readChairmanPriority` in `src/work-gate.ts`, recorded by `src/failure-recorders.ts`, #730 and #4437) reads who added the label from the row's history: a label added by any login other than the chairman's is IGNORED (the row is offered as its other labels say and nothing is started for it), the incident is recorded once per row and actor under the failure-ledger kind `chairman-label-not-chairman`, and `ceo` is ordered to take the label off if it should not stand.
classes.guardNote: The guard removes the effect, not the act: nothing stops a login putting the label on, and the label stays until someone removes it. The ledger holds seven rows from one login (`a11ign-ai-leads`) between 20:11Z and 20:27Z on 2026-10-10 (a11ign/a11ign#4874, #4877, #4879+#4883, #4880, #4882, #4885, #4887), so it is a repeat; why that login added it, and whether a session was doing so on purpose, has not been read. Instances are ledger lines, not closed rows.

classes.name: Model routing through the provider costs more than the deterministic fallback it replaced: over the last 20 routes that name the fallback's would-be route, the provider's mean rung is above the fallback's.
classes.guardNote: The detector is in force and the class is not stopped. `routeCostReading` and `routeCostEvents` in a11ign/agent-org `src/engineer-route.ts` (a11ign#4764) compare the last `GUARD_DECISIONS` (20) `via jev` routes with the route the fallback would have taken and, when the provider's mean rung is strictly dearer, record one `route-costlier-than-fallback` line a day in the failure ledger; it reads and does not switch the provider off. The ledger holds two distinct refs (`model-routing-vs-fallback@2026-10-10` at 09:40Z, `@2026-10-11` at 00:06Z), so this is a repeat. Both predate agent-org v0.151.0 (cut 2026-10-11T00:42Z), the first release carrying the route as one choice put to Jev with uneven thresholds (a11ign#4904), so whether that change closes the class has not been read: the next ledger line after v0.151.0 is the reading. Whether the provider should be switched off while it reads dearer has not been decided. Instances are ledger lines, not closed rows.

classes.name: An announcement asks the chairman something, or an ask has no row or no record, so the messaging channel drifts back into the one chat it replaced.
classes.guard: `deliver()` in `src/messaging/core.ts` of a11ign/agent-org refuses an announcement whose text asks the chairman something, before any send, and writes the refusal to the failure ledger under `messaging-audience-misuse` (`refuseAsking`, agent-org#1222, merged as PR 1237 on 2026-10-12). It is in force because the flag `messaging.refuseAskingAnnouncements` is ON (switch row a11ign#5297; `machinery:flag list` reads it ON, verdict `watching`, set 2026-10-12T19:43:25Z). The ask predicate is `asksSomething` with `markersOf` in `src/messaging/audit.ts`, shared with the detector `auditMessaging` (a11ign#4746, agent-org#654), so the guard and the detector cannot disagree about what an ask is. The two ledger occurrences (providerMessageId 4 and 140) were FALSE FLAGS: release announcements quoting an `answer:` label, cleared by the release-marker exemption of agent-org#999. The detector records only; the refusal is the stop.

classes.name: A role declared `github-apps` makes calls and never as its app, so its calls go to the shared account unnoticed.
classes.guard: `tickAppRoleSilent` in agent-org `src/host-units.ts` runs on every tick of an agent host, after `tickRerenderGhWrapper` re-renders the `gh` wrapper (agent-org#790, measured in a11ign/a11ign#4906). It asks `appRoleSilent` in `src/app-role-silent.ts` over each account's call ledger, and files each silent role through `recordFailures` as one `app-role-silent` line, a standing episode being one line however many ticks see it (`src/app-role-silent.test.ts`). The detector's report carries the failed mint's reason, exit status and time (agent-org#1682): its stderr line reads `the mint failed at <time>: <reason> (exit <n>)`, or `no app-token incident in the ledger`.
classes.guardNote: Detector only: it records the silence and does not repair it. The repair is the wrapper re-render that runs first in the same tick, so a repeat means the re-render did not take effect (a failed mint falls back to the shared account by design, or refuses once agent-org#1666 lands). A repeat's mint reason is on the host's stderr line in the journal, not in the failure ledger, whose dedupe key and event are unchanged. A host with no user systemd reads nothing (`asked` in `jsonReport`), so this detector is blind there.

classes.name: A tool changes underneath the org on its own schedule, and the first symptom is an agent stuck on an interactive prompt.
classes.guard: Two readings, two guards. (1) THE USAGE-LIMIT MENU (`Stop and wait for limit to reset` and `Switch to usage credits` on screen) is a DATED WAIT, never a decision and never an option taken: `gate.accountLimitPause` (agent-org `src/account-limit.ts`, agent-org#1307, flag ON since 2026-10-13T20:52:59Z) records the reset hour it names, and `limitMenuTick` in `src/wake.ts` (agent-org#1412) sends `esc` to a blocked seat parked on that menu once the reset has passed, found by `isLimitMenu` in `src/worker-state.ts`, which needs both options on screen. The usage-credits option is never chosen. (2) A TOOL MOVE that shows a dialog: `agent-org agent-tool:update` in agent-org `src/agent-tool-update.ts` (agent-org#462 and #665, `.acceptance/`) refuses while a seat that runs a tool it is about to move is mid-turn, switches off the Codex daemon's own update loop, moves the tools and reads each back, starts a Codex reviewer and a Claude worker in a scratch pane, reverts the whole set when either reaches a dialog, and files one incident per failed smoke with the pane text. It is not a guard for reading (1). It is an operator command, not a tick: no caller in `src` runs it besides its registration in `src/commands.ts`, so a move not run through it is not covered; the revert covers only the tools that run moved; and the incident is written after the revert, so it names a drift already undone. GAP, NOT CLOSED BY THIS ENTRY: `raisePaneDialogs` in agent-org `src/pane-dialog.ts` (agent-org#463) has no limit-menu exclusion (`isLimitMenu` is read only by `limitMenuTick` and `tellBlocked`), so a seat parked on the limit menu is still raised as a `tool-drift-interactive-prompt` DECISION order to its owner with the question and choices quoted. The ledger's occurrences from 2026-10-13T20:39Z to 2026-10-15T07:01Z were raised through that path, four of them before the flag was switched on. The exclusion is filed as a11ign/agent-org#1481 (ready; no `isLimitMenu` in `src/pane-dialog.ts` at agent-org `origin/main` f494fc41); until it merges the decision-order raise is not stopped, and this entry does not claim that it is.

classes.name: A holder's claim shelves the ready rows behind it for hours, or a pull request and a row wait on each other, and nobody is told.
classes.guard: `blockingImpactOrders` in agent-org `src/work-gate/causes/org-health-resolver-defects.ts`, called from `src/work-gate.ts` on every gate tick, runs `blockingImpactTick` in `src/blocking-impact.ts` (a11ign/a11ign#4602): it counts the ready rows each holder shelves by an overlap reason, and raises one `lock-gridlock` incident per holder per episode once that reaches `BLOCKING_MIN_ROWS` for `BLOCKING_MIN_MINUTES`. A circular wait is woken to its pull request's holder, then escalated to `orchestrator` once it still stands (agent-org#5009). The holder is told what its claim shelves by `blastTail` (a11ign/a11ign#4605), and a repository's sweep past its box is released by `src/sweep-window.ts` (a11ign/a11ign#4603, `sweep-overrun`). THE ESCALATION RULE IS IN FORCE (agent-org#1426, merged as agent-org#1468): a fired episode still standing `BLOCKING_ESCALATE_MINUTES` (60) after it fired is put to `product-manager` once, with the ways out, and its held rows are written to. It releases no claim and writes no second ledger line. Before that rule the detector was a notice, and it DID NOT STOP THE CLASS: the three occurrences (`worker-5100` 2026-10-11, `worker-5125` 2026-10-11, `worker-agent-org-1185` 2026-10-13) each raised one incident and one wake (`wake-ledger`), and the shelving went on. Still not covered: nothing here frees a shelved row except a sweep, and a shelving whose reason names no holder (a branch already on origin, a template gap, a declared wait) is dropped, not counted, so its holder is never told. The record is read from `blocking-impact.json`, so a gap between ticks (a restart, an outage) ends an episode rather than being counted as shelved.

classes.name: A row claim is refused, and the refusals repeat, so the org cannot make the claims its rows need.
classes.guard: A refusal that is the claim guard working is written `claim-guard-held`, not `claim-refused`, so it is no occurrence of this class: `GUARD_HELD_REFUSALS` in agent-org `src/row-claim.ts` (agent-org#1262) names the worktree cap, a B4 overlap, an existing tree or branch, a rate-limited read and a stale rule copy, and a refusal not yet named there still counts, by design. The class counts its refs from `countedSince` (agent-org#1316, `src/class-repeat.ts`): a ref written before the guard was in force is the defect it fixed, not a repeat. The storm reading (`claimRefusalStormReading`, signal 26, agent-org `src/org-health.ts`, agent-org#889) reads the `claim-refused` lines `recordClaimRefusal` writes for each refusal the claim command prints (agent-org#972), and trips when more than `CLAIM_REFUSAL_STORM_REFUSALS` fall in `CLAIM_REFUSAL_STORM_MINUTES`.

classes.name: Claude Code's built-in safety check denies a command it cannot read (a nested `bash -c` carrying `$`, or a removal whose target is a variable), and the session sits idle on the denied command.
classes.guard: `scripts/claude-hooks/refuse-unreadable-command.ts`, a PreToolUse hook on Bash wired in `.claude/settings.json` (so every role that runs in this repository has it, the ceo's included), refuses the two shapes the six denied commands share and prints the rewrite; `scripts/claude-hooks/refuse-unreadable-command.test.ts` runs the six verbatim commands in `scripts/fixtures/safety-check-denied-commands.json` through it and goes red when the guard is removed or always fires. The ledger naming of the shapes is a11ign/agent-org#1275.
classes.guardNote: Five of six denied commands contain NO removal: each is a nested `bash -c` whose string carries a `$` expansion; the sixth is `rm -rf "$S/$m"`. The two shapes are inferred from those six, not the check's own rule. The hook only reaches a session whose working directory is this repository or one of its worktrees; a session elsewhere (a11ign/agent-org, control, lab) keeps the engineer brief's rule and nothing else. The detector `safetyCheckDenialEvents` in agent-org `src/safety-check-denial-incident.ts` names a shape only for `rm` (every other command is `other`): adding these shapes is a change in agent-org, filed as a11ign/agent-org#1275. It counts only denials left in a transcript, so a command the chairman approved leaves nothing to count.

classes.name: The gate holds a red pull request for a shared-failure incident and then releases it, so one failure still wakes a worker for each pull request that shares it.
classes.guard: THE STOP: a11ign/agent-org#1559 (merged as ef2fb8c, closing agent-org#1557) removed the `expired` release in `standingOf` (`src/ci-failure-class.ts` in agent-org). That release woke every held pull request of an OPEN incident row that nobody had claimed, 15 minutes after the row opened (`HOLD_MAX_MS`). An open row now holds its pull requests until it closes, and the gate logs `ci-shared-failure: incident #n has been open ... no worker is woken` instead. The releases left are `closed` (the incident ended) and `unrecorded`. The count is still in force: `sharedFailureWakes` in agent-org `src/org-retro.ts` reads the `ci-shared-failure:` lines (`SHARED_FAILURE_HELD_KIND`), counting a pull request once per window however many holds it had. NOT COVERED BY THIS ENTRY: the second count, `shared-failure-not-same` (`SHARED_FAILURE_NOT_SAME_KIND`), whose detector in `src/org-retro.ts` is its own row, so it is not yet a reading of this class.

classes.name: A claimed worker's turn is ended on the stop hook's bound: the hook refused twice for one row with no pull request and no declared state, and the stop was then allowed.
classes.guard: THE LEDGER LINE, AND THE BOUND'S DECLARATION. Agent-org `src/worker-stop-hook.ts` (agent-org#853, MAX_REFUSALS=2) refuses a worker's stop twice for a row with no pull request and no declared state. At the bound the stop is allowed, and the hook does two things: it makes the `blocked` declaration on the worker's behalf, through `worker:state blocked`'s own path (`applyBlocked`, `writeDeclaration`), so the row carries `answer:product-manager` and a reason and the gate reads it; and it writes one `stop-hook-bound` line to the failure ledger, which is the detector this entry counts. The declaration is agent-org#1488, merged as `326bdbf7` (closed 2026-10-15T16:07Z); on agent-org `origin/main` it is `declareAtBound` in `worker-stop-hook.ts`. The ledger line is now a count of bound stops that were routed, not of silent ones.
classes.guardNote: THE BOUND IS THE CLASS, AND THE GAP THAT REMAINS IS THE OFFER. The refusal (agent-org#853) does stop a turn that could still be satisfied. At MAX_REFUSALS the stop is allowed, and the bound is sticky: the count stays at 2 until a satisfied turn clears it, so every later stop of that row is allowed without a refusal and writes another ledger line (a11ign#5466). Measured 2026-10-15 from the failure ledger and `worker-stop-hook/` counts, before agent-org#1488 merged: ten `stop-hook-bound` lines over five rows (a11ign#4405 twice, agent-org#1302 twice, a11ign#5306 once, a11ign#5466 three times, a11ign#5155 twice). On those rows the allowance left no declaration and no pull request, the state the hook was built to prevent (a11ign#4957); the bound now declares, so a row that reaches it is routed. Both bounds on a11ign#5155 came 53 s and 34 s after a fresh wake-ledger delivery. What remains open is WHY engineers reach the bound: a lane-owner row spawned onto an engineer seat that cannot reach what the row needs is refused its stop until the bound, and the declaration then routes it to product-manager instead of completing it. Such a row belongs to the orchestrator one-shot lane (agent-org#1527), and the ledger line counts those cases.
